content: The Meningococcal Group B Vaccine, also known by its brand name BEXSERO®, is a two-dose vaccine approved by the FDA for the prevention of invasive disease caused by Neisseria meningitidis serogroup B. It is specifically indicated for individuals aged 10 through 25 years. The vaccine works by stimulating the production of antibodies that target specific proteins on the surface of the bacteria, including NHBA, NadA, fHbp, and PorA P1.4. These antibodies facilitate complement-mediated, antibody-dependent killing of the bacteria. Administration and Dosage The vaccine is administered intramuscularly as two 0.5 mL doses, spaced at least one month apart. It is injected into the deltoid muscle of the upper arm. If the vaccine cannot be resuspended or if particulate matter or discoloration is observed, it should not be used. The vaccine is for intramuscular use only and should not be administered intravenously. Contraindications The vaccine is contraindicated in individuals with hypersensitivity or severe allergic reactions to any component of the vaccine or to a previous dose of the vaccine. Warnings and Precautions Anaphylaxis: Medical treatment and observation should be readily available in case of an anaphylactic reaction following vaccination. Syncope: Latex Sensitivity: The tip caps of the pre-filled syringes contain natural rubber latex, which may cause allergic reactions in latex-sensitive individuals. Immunocompromised Individuals: Those with altered immune function may have a reduced immune response to the vaccine. Incomplete Protection: The vaccine may not protect all recipients or provide protection against all serogroup B strains. Adverse Reactions The most common adverse reactions observed in clinical trials include: Pain at the injection site (≥83%) Muscle pain (myalgia) (≥48%) Redness at the injection site (erythema) (≥45%) Fatigue (≥35%) Headache (≥33%) Swelling or hardening at the injection site (induration) (≥28%) Nausea (≥18%) Joint pain (arthralgia) (≥13%) Severe myalgia was reported in 3-7% of participants, and severe pain was reported by 8% of university students in one study. Serious adverse events were rare, occurring in 0.8% of vaccine recipients compared to 0.5% in control groups. One case of anaphylaxis was reported within 30 minutes of vaccination. Clinical Studies The vaccine's effectiveness was evaluated by measuring serum bactericidal activity using human complement (hSBA) against three representative serogroup B strains. In clinical trials, the vaccine demonstrated the ability to elicit a robust immune response in individuals aged 10 through 25 years. However, its effectiveness against diverse serogroup B strains has not been fully established. Use in Specific Populations Pregnancy: Animal studies in rabbits showed no evidence of harm to the fetus or impaired fertility. However, there are no adequate studies in pregnant women. The vaccine should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. A pregnancy registry is available to monitor outcomes (1-877-683-4732). Nursing Mothers: It is unknown whether the vaccine is excreted in human milk, so caution is advised. Pediatric Use: The vaccine is not approved for use in children under 10 years of age. Geriatric Use: The safety and effectiveness of the vaccine have not been established in individuals over 65 years of age. Immunocompromised Patients: The immune response may be reduced in these individuals. Storage and Handling The vaccine should be stored in a refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C) and protected from light. It should not be frozen, and any vaccine that has been frozen must be discarded. The vaccine should not be used after its expiration date. Drug Interactions There is insufficient data on the safety and immunogenicity of administering the Meningococcal Group B Vaccine concurrently with other recommended adolescent vaccines. Mechanism of Action The vaccine induces the production of antibodies targeting specific proteins on the surface of Neisseria meningitidis serogroup B. These antibodies facilitate the killing of the bacteria through complement-mediated mechanisms. The vaccine's effectiveness depends on the antigenic similarity between the vaccine and bacterial antigens, as well as the level of antigen expression on the bacterial surface. Pregnancy Registry Healthcare providers are encouraged to register pregnant women who receive the vaccine by calling 1-877-683-4732. Postmarketing Experience Adverse events reported postmarketing include: General Disorders: Blisters at or around the injection site. Immune System Disorders: Allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, rash, and eye swelling. Nervous System Disorders: Syncope and vasovagal responses to injection. Patient Counseling Patients should be informed about the importance of completing the vaccination series, the potential for adverse reactions, and the availability of a pregnancy registry for those vaccinated during pregnancy. Vaccine Information Statements are available at the CDC website (www.cdc.gov/vaccines). Brand Name The vaccine is marketed under the brand name BEXSERO®. Summary The Meningococcal Group B Vaccine is a two-dose intramuscular vaccine designed to prevent invasive disease caused by Neisseria meningitidis serogroup B. It is generally well-tolerated, with pain at the injection site being the most common adverse reaction. While it is effective in eliciting an immune response, it may not protect against all serogroup B strains or in all individuals.
